newsitem.title: USA: Spector ups 1997 aluminum market deficit forecast.
newsitem.headline: Spector ups 1997 aluminum market deficit forecast.

text.p: Western world aluminum market supply/demand deficit this year will be wider than previously thought because producers are wary of restarting idled capacity too soon, industry analyst Stewart Spector said.
"It appears that major producers have finally learned their supply/demand lessons well," Spector said in his latest industry report.

This year's supply and demand deficit could approximate 835,000 tons, some 270,000 tons more than Spector previously forecast because major restarts of idled capacity now did not appear likely mid-year but would probably happen in the third or fourth quarter.
Spector said there was some 900,000 tons of idled capacity at major producers. Although he did not name them, Alcoa, Reynolds Metals, and Alcan own the bulk of spare capacity.
"These large producers are now significant net ingot buyers," Spector said.
It was more profitable to go out an buy the extra metal they needed rather than produce as much as they can which risked pushing ingot prices down, Spector said.
In the first quarter, despite strong demand, producers and consumers either reduced or added very little metal to their inventories.

As almost all suppliers and their customers use LME to hedge prices three years or more forward, once hedged there is not the same urgency to carry additional safety stocks as there was in the past, Spector said.
